exposure: Changing national fertility policy in China ('three-child' policy)
cohort: 20,334 births with a gestational age more than 28 weeks
finding: The 'three-child' policy in China did not increase birth rates and was associated with an increase in the proportion of multiparous women and women with advanced maternal age, along with higher rates of premature birth and low birth weight.
mod_finding: The caesarean section rates showed a declining trend, while the assisted birth rates were progressively rising, especially among primiparous women.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was measured and analyzed.
